moduleTitle: Configuring and managing projects in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Explain the process of generating base test code using the command line interface (CLI) to streamline test execution.
Describe how to manage project users, invite teammates, and assign roles to ensure smooth team collaboration.
Explain how to oversee projects and users at the company level, managing multiple projects and teammates efficiently.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Generating base test code with the CLI

elements.description: On the Settings > CLI page, clicking CI generates base code (containing your token and project ID) for running tests remotely on a CI platform; clicking Local generates the equivalent base code for running tests on your own machine (web only — this opens a local browser). Under CI, you can also pick a CI Platform and a Grid to further tailor the generated command.

Whichever mode you pick, Testim generates a ready-to-run CLI command pre-filled with your token and project ID — click Copy to grab it for your shell or CI pipeline, rather than typing the whole command (and looking up the token/project ID) by hand every time.

bulletPoints: Settings > CLI → CI (remote/CI platform) or Local (your own machine) → generates a ready command with token + project ID pre-filled.
Copy button grabs the command directly — no manual lookup of token/project ID needed.

elements.description: The Project teammates screen (via the Users icon in the main navigation) lists everyone currently assigned to the project. Inviting is done by entering each teammate's work email (followed by space or Enter), then clicking Invite.

Any team member can invite new project teammates. A project owner has broader authority: they can remove teammates and add/remove other project owners — a distinction worth knowing since 'can invite' and 'can remove/promote' are not the same permission level.

bulletPoints: Invite teammates: Users icon → enter work email(s) → Invite.
Any member can invite; only an owner can remove teammates or add/remove other owners.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Overseeing projects and users at the company level

elements.term: Tracking who worked on a project
elements.description: Two complementary ways to check which individuals have worked on a particular project: the Users section, which displays which user is associated with which project; and the Insights Dashboard, which surfaces an identifier that lets you track any user who has worked on a given project — giving both a static membership view and an activity-based view.

elements.text: This is NOT limited to only the projects a user has personally been assigned to, and it does NOT require integrating a separate third-party project-management tool — both of those would defeat the point of built-in company-level oversight.

bulletPoints: Users section: shows user ↔ project associations directly.
Insights Dashboard: an identifier for tracking any user who has worked on a project — not limited to your own assigned projects, no external tool needed.

elements.description: A toggle in the project's pull request settings that prevents writing directly to the Master branch and/or other selected branches (making them read-only) — changes must go through a pull request instead of a direct commit.

If Master is protected, 'Allow Auto-improve on master' can still be enabled so the Auto-improve locator feature keeps working even on a protected branch. 'Require approving reviewer' can be turned on per-branch to mandate a review before a pull request merges. Only the project owner or company owner can change these settings, and they're a professional-plan-only feature.

bulletPoints: Protect Master from changes = prevents direct writes to Master (and/or other selected branches) — changes must go through a PR.
Allow Auto-improve on master: keeps Auto-improve working even when Master is protected.
Only project/company owners can configure this; professional plan only.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming any team member can remove another teammate
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting a regular project member to be able to remove someone from the project the same way they can invite someone.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inviting is open to any team member, but removing teammates or adding/removing project owners is restricted to project owners.

examPitfalls.title: Manually typing the CLI command instead of generating it
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Hand-typing the testim CLI command, including looking up the token and project ID from elsewhere.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use Settings > CLI (CI or Local) to generate the base command with your token and project ID pre-filled, then Copy it — rather than reconstructing it manually.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing 'Protect Master from changes' with deleting or locking out all edits
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming the protection setting deletes the master branch or makes it completely uneditable by anyone under any circumstance.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: It only prevents direct writes — changes still happen through pull requests, and Auto-improve can still be allowed to run against a protected master if that toggle is enabled.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Who can remove a teammate from the project in Testim?
practiceQuiz.hint: Inviting and removing are different permission levels.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Only a project owner can remove teammates or add/remove other project owners — any team member can invite, but removal is restricted to owners.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can you run your tests using the CLI in Testim?

options.text: By executing tests directly from the Testim dashboard
By integrating tests with your continuous integration (CI) platform or using your local shell
By using only the CI Integration option
By downloading a separate Testim CLI application

practiceQuiz.hint: Settings > CLI gives you exactly two modes to generate the base command for.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Settings > CLI page offers CI (run remotely via a CI platform) and Local (run on your own machine/shell) — both are valid ways to run tests via the CLI, not just one exclusively, and it's not run from the dashboard or a separate downloaded app (it's the same npm-installed @testim/testim-cli package).

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can a user check which individual has working on a particular project?

options.text: The users sections displays which user is associated with which particular project
Users can only check the projects that they have been assigned
The Insights Dashboard shows an identifier through which any user that has worked on a particular project can be tracked
Users will need to integrate another project management software into Testim to check actions of other users on projects

practiceQuiz.hint: Two built-in views: a static membership list, and an activity-tracking identifier — no external tool needed.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Users section directly shows user-to-project associations, and the Insights Dashboard provides an identifier to track any user who has worked on a project — this isn't limited to a user's own assigned projects, and no separate project-management integration is required.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the "Protect Master from changes" setting do in Testim's pull requests settings?

options.text: Allows changes to the master branch
Prevents writing directly to the master branch
Makes the master branch editable by all users

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a branch-protection toggle, like read-only mode.
practiceQuiz.rationale: 'Protect branches from changes' (applied here to Master) prevents writing directly to that branch — changes must go through a pull request instead. It doesn't allow direct edits, delete anything, or open the branch up to all users.

quickRecap.value: Settings > CLI → CI or Local → ready command with token/project ID, Copy button.
Users icon → work email(s) → Invite (any team member can do this).
Users section (associations) + Insights Dashboard (activity identifier) — no external tool needed.
Prevents direct writes to Master; changes go through a PR. Owner-only, professional plan.
